name: The Camino Francés
subtitle: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Santiago de Compostela, 780 km
source_note: About 780 km from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port to Santiago de Compostela, in four stages. Distances follow common guidebook figures and vary by a few kilometres with the variant taken.

stages.name: Burgos to León, across the Meseta

events.title: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port
events.body: A stamp in your pilgrim's credential, a scallop shell on your pack, and a cobbled street running downhill to the Porte d'Espagne. 780 km to Santiago. The first day is the hardest: it crosses the Pyrenees.

events.title: Over the mountain or through the valley?
events.body: Two ways into Spain. The Route Napoléon goes over the top; the Valcarlos road follows the valley, and it is the one to take when snow closes the pass.

options.label: Route Napoléon
options.outcome: You climb into the clouds with the vultures and the sheep. On a clear day you can see all the way back to the plains of France.

options.label: Valcarlos road
options.outcome: Chestnut woods, a river beside you and a village for coffee. The climb waits for you at the end, in smaller pieces.

events.title: Orisson
events.body: The last refuge before the pass. Water, a bench, and the valley falling away below.

events.title: The climb to the pass
events.body: Well over a thousand metres of climbing in a single morning. Lean into it and keep a steady rhythm.

challenge.success: The Col de Lepoeder, at about 1,450 metres. Downhill from here, for today.
challenge.failure: You stop more often than you meant to. The mountain does not mind, and neither should you.
challenge.note: No incline? Push the pace instead: the app checks speed if your treadmill does not report incline.

events.title: Into Spain
events.body: A stone marker and a cattle grid: you have crossed the border without noticing.

events.title: Roncesvalles
events.body: A great stone collegiate church in a fold of the mountain, a pilgrims' blessing in the evening, and a dormitory full of people who all started today.

events.title: Zubiri
events.body: A medieval bridge over the Arga, and the first blisters being compared on its parapet.

events.title: Pamplona
events.body: Over the Magdalena bridge and through the Portal de Francia into the walled city. In July the bulls run these streets; today it is only walkers.

events.title: Alto del Perdón
events.body: A long climb to a ridge lined with wind turbines. The wind up there pushes back.

challenge.success: On the ridge stands a line of iron pilgrims. Their inscription says this is where the way of the wind crosses the way of the stars.
challenge.failure: You reach the top slowly, with the wind in your face. You still reach it.

events.title: Puente la Reina
events.body: Its Romanesque bridge has carried pilgrims over the Arga for nine centuries. The route from Aragón has joined yours: one road from now on.

events.title: Estella
events.body: A town that grew up around the pilgrim road, full of Romanesque churches.

events.title: The wine fountain at Irache
events.body: The winery beside the monastery of Irache has put a tap in its wall: one side water, the other red wine, free for walkers. Moderation is advised.

events.title: Los Arcos
events.body: A plain square, a lavish church, and a long afternoon in the shade.

events.title: Logroño
events.body: The capital of La Rioja. In the evening the narrow streets around Calle Laurel fill with people going from one tapas bar to the next.

events.title: Vineyards
events.body: Rows of vines to the horizon, and red earth that stains your boots.

events.title: Nájera
events.body: Red cliffs above the river, with caves dug into them.

events.title: Santo Domingo de la Calzada
events.body: A live hen and rooster are kept inside the cathedral, in memory of a medieval miracle about a pilgrim wrongly hanged. They are very calm about it.

events.title: Belorado
events.body: Into the province of Burgos. The fields turn from vines to wheat.

events.title: The Montes de Oca
events.body: Oak and pine forest that pilgrims once feared for its bandits. Today it is just long and quiet. Keep moving.

challenge.success: You come out of the trees with the afternoon still ahead of you.
challenge.failure: The forest stretches on. You arrive late, but you arrive.

events.title: San Juan de Ortega
events.body: A monastery in a clearing, founded by a saint who spent his life making this road safer, with bridges and a hospice.

events.title: Atapuerca
events.body: Just off the path, caves where some of the oldest human remains in Europe were found. Pilgrims are recent visitors here.

events.title: Burgos
events.body: A Gothic cathedral of white stone, all spires and lace. Stage one of four is done: 290 km behind you. Take a rest day if you can.

events.title: Onto the Meseta
events.body: The high plateau of Castile: wheat, sky, and a path running straight to the horizon. Some love it, some dread it.

events.title: Hornillos del Camino
events.body: A single street of stone houses, built along the road because of the road.

events.title: Hontanas
events.body: A village hidden in a fold of the plain. You only see the church tower when you are almost there.

events.title: The arch of San Antón
events.body: The road passes right under the ruined arch of a medieval monastery. Its monks cared for pilgrims struck by a fever that made them burn.

events.title: Castrojeriz
events.body: A long village wrapped around the foot of a castle hill.

events.title: Alto de Mostelares
events.body: A short, steep climb out of the valley, then the plateau opens again.

challenge.success: From the top, the Meseta in every direction, cut by the path you just walked.
challenge.failure: You stop halfway to catch your breath. The view is just as good from there.

events.title: The Canal de Castilla
events.body: An 18th-century canal, with a towpath that walks you into Frómista.

events.title: Frómista
events.body: San Martín, one of the purest Romanesque churches in Spain, stands alone in its square.

events.title: Carrión de los Condes
events.body: Last shop for a while: the next stretch has no village for about 17 km.

events.title: The Roman road
events.body: Seventeen kilometres of straight gravel on an old Roman road, with nothing to hide behind. Carry water and keep a steady pace.

challenge.success: Calzadilla de la Cueza appears in its hollow, and its café is open.
challenge.failure: The heat slows you down. You make it, with an empty bottle.

events.title: Sahagún
events.body: Brick churches in the Mudéjar style, and roughly the halfway point of the Camino. The town gives walkers a certificate to prove it.

events.title: Mansilla de las Mulas
events.body: Old town walls, and the last night before the city.

events.title: León
events.body: A cathedral made mostly of light, with some of the finest medieval stained glass in Europe. Stage two is done, 475 km behind you. The Meseta is over.

events.title: Hospital de Órbigo
events.body: A long medieval bridge where, in 1434, a knight is said to have held the crossing against all comers in a month of jousts, for love.

events.title: Astorga
events.body: Roman walls, a fairy-tale bishop's palace by Gaudí, and a long tradition of chocolate making.

events.title: Into the Montes de León
events.body: The path climbs again, through broom and heather, into the wind.

challenge.success: Foncebadón: a village that was almost abandoned, and came back to life thanks to walkers.
challenge.failure: The climb takes everything you have today. Foncebadón waits for you all the same.

events.title: Cruz de Ferro
events.body: A small iron cross on a tall wooden pole, standing on a mound of stones. Pilgrims carry a stone from home all the way here and leave it. At about 1,500 m, this is the highest point of the Camino Francés.

events.title: Ponferrada
events.body: A Templar castle guarding the bridge over the river Sil.

events.title: Villafranca del Bierzo
events.body: Its church has a Door of Forgiveness: in the Middle Ages, pilgrims too sick to go on could earn their pilgrimage here.

events.title: The climb to O Cebreiro
events.body: The last big climb, from chestnut groves up to the hills of Galicia. Often in fog.

challenge.success: You come over the top into a stone village in the clouds.
challenge.failure: Slowly, with stops. The fog hides how far you still had to go, which helps.

events.title: Into Galicia
events.body: A granite marker with a scallop shell. From here, stone markers count down the distance to Santiago.

events.title: O Cebreiro
events.body: Round stone houses with thatched roofs, and a pre-Romanesque church. Its parish priest started painting the yellow arrows that now guide walkers along the whole Camino.

events.title: Samos or San Xil?
events.body: After Triacastela the way splits for a day and joins again in Sarria.

options.label: Via Samos
options.detail: Longer, along a river, past a great monastery.
options.outcome: There has been a monastery at Samos for well over a thousand years. You walk in under its walls.

options.label: Via San Xil
options.outcome: Small hamlets, chestnut trees and stone walls. You meet more cows than people.

events.title: Sarria
events.body: Many pilgrims start here: the Compostela is given to those who walk at least the last 100 km. Stage three is done, and the path gets busy.

events.title: 100 km to go
events.body: The most photographed marker on the Camino: one hundred kilometres to Santiago.

events.title: Portomarín
events.body: When a reservoir flooded the old town in the 1960s, its church was taken apart and rebuilt, stone by stone, on the hill above.

events.title: Hórreos
events.body: Stone granaries on legs, with a cross on the roof, beside every farm.

events.title: Palas de Rei
events.body: Rain, then sun, then rain. Galicia does both in the same hour.

events.title: Melide
events.body: The town is known for its octopus, boiled and served on wooden plates with paprika and olive oil.

events.title: Arzúa
events.body: Cheese country: a soft, mild cheese with the town's name on it.

events.title: Eucalyptus
events.body: Tall eucalyptus woods. The air smells like a cough sweet.

events.title: The last push
events.body: The city is close and your legs know it. One more effort.

challenge.success: Monte do Gozo, the Mount of Joy: the cathedral's spires on the skyline.
challenge.failure: You go slowly up the last hill. The spires are there anyway.

events.title: Monte do Gozo
events.body: The first view of the cathedral. Tradition says medieval pilgrims raced each other up here to see it first.

events.title: Santiago de Compostela
events.body: A bagpiper under the archway, then the Praza do Obradoiro and the cathedral's façade. 780 km, every one of them walked. The Pilgrim's Office has your Compostela.
